newsitem.title: UK: UK details competition law plans, MMC head leaves.
newsitem.headline: UK details competition law plans, MMC head leaves.

text.p: Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett on Thursday published draft legislation to reform competition law aimed at tightening control of anti-competitive behaviour.

A new Competition Commission will be set up and will take on the existing functions of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, whose chairman, Sir Graeme Odgers, said he would resign at the end of this year, 15 months earlier than planned.

The Labour government in May announced it planned a bill on competition, and on Thursday Beckett said she would bring forward legislation in the autumn to introduce a prohibition-based approach to competition law.
Odgers said his decision to leave the MMC resulted from his wish "to end his substantive career in the private, as opposed to the public, sector."
He said he had indicated his intentions to Beckett's predecessor, but the election in May and then the present government's review of competition policy intervened.

Odgers said, "I strongly support the proposals being put forward by Mrs Beckett...for the new Competition Bill and for the creation of the Competition Commission which will embrace the MMC and the Appeals Body for the new prohibition system".

Beckett said he accepted Odgers' resignation with regret, and said a competition would be held for his successor. She said the new chairman of the MMC was expected to become the first chairman of the Competition Commission.

The new law will include prohibitions based on European Union articles against anti-competitive agreements and cartels and against abuse of a dominant position. It will involve penalties in the form of fines and an appeal procedure.
